subsystems.name: Expert networks
subsystems.role: many small feed-forward networks, each expected to specialise in different patterns; only a few run for any given token.
parts: two or three linear layers per expert

subsystems.name: Router (gating network)
subsystems.role: scores every expert for each token and picks the top few to run.

subsystems.name: Shared experts
subsystems.role: a small set of experts that always run, absorbing common knowledge so the routed experts can specialise.

subsystems.name: Load-balancing mechanism
subsystems.role: stops the router sending everything to a handful of experts, which would waste the rest.
parts: per-expert bias adjustments or an auxiliary loss

subsystems.name: Attention and representation layers
subsystems.role: understand context; in this family the key/value cache is compressed into a low-rank latent to cut memory.

subsystems.name: Distributed training and serving stack
subsystems.role: spreads experts across many accelerators and shuttles tokens to whichever expert needs them.

buildSteps.title: Design the sparsity budget
buildSteps.detail: Choose layer count, how many experts per layer, how finely they are split, and how many are active per token — this sets the cost/quality trade-off.

buildSteps.title: Write the expert and router code
buildSteps.detail: Implement the expert feed-forward blocks, the top-k gate, and the shared-expert path in a training framework such as PyTorch.

buildSteps.title: Add balancing and stability tricks
buildSteps.detail: Bias terms nudged up or down according to each expert's load, plus careful initialisation, keep training from collapsing onto few experts.

buildSteps.title: Partition across accelerators
buildSteps.detail: Experts are placed on different devices; tokens are dispatched to their chosen experts and results returned, so fast interconnects matter more than raw compute.

buildSteps.title: Pre-train on a large text corpus
buildSteps.detail: The model learns to predict the next token at scale, with the router gradually sorting itself into specialisms.

buildSteps.title: Post-train and align
buildSteps.detail: Supervised fine-tuning and preference-based reinforcement learning shape the base model into a helpful assistant.

buildSteps.title: Quantise and serve
buildSteps.detail: Weights are stored at low precision and an inference engine batches requests so that only the needed experts are loaded and run per token.

prerequisites.why: experts replace the feed-forward blocks of an otherwise standard transformer.
the core idea of routing tokens to a subset of parameters is well established and now widely reproduced.
every token must be shipped to its experts and back; slow links make the savings disappear.
eight-bit formats cut memory and bandwidth enough to make very large sparse models economic.
getting experts to specialise usefully rather than collapse is still an active, partly empirical problem.
thousands of accelerators must run for weeks without a failure ending the run.

pathway.milestone: open-weight sparse models served cheaply by many providers
pathway.unlocks: frontier-class capability at a fraction of dense-model inference cost.

pathway.milestone: finer expert granularity and learned, hardware-aware routing
pathway.unlocks: better quality per unit of compute and less wasted communication.

pathway.milestone: sparse models extended to images, audio and long agentic tasks
pathway.unlocks: one economical model handling many modalities.

pathway.milestone: experts that can be swapped or updated independently after training
pathway.unlocks: cheap specialisation and patching without retraining the whole network.
